issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces entry to the event {dist(a_\delta X_0,\mc{R}_\delta)+\sqrt{h_\delta}\|z\|\le \rho_\delta} and proves dist(a_\delta X_0,\mc{R}_\delta)\le \rho_\delta/2, so the Gaussian event should be {\|z\|^2\le \rho_\delta^2/(4h_\delta)}. It instead uses {\|z\|^2\le \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta}. Then, using only the lower bound r_t=\Omega(h_t^2) up to subexponential factors and \rho_t=\Theta(r_t), it chooses \delta so that \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta is below the LMI threshold. But the LMI bound P(\|z\|^2\le threshold)\ge 1-h_\delta^\zeta transfers to P(\|z\|^2\le \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta) only when \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta\ge threshold, the opposite inequality. With \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta\to 0 the event has probability tending to 0, so the claimed high-probability entry is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must choose a tube radius \rho_\delta large enough (e.g., a data-dependent constant) while proving r_\delta\ge \rho_\delta, and use the correct Gaussian tail inequality P(\|z\|^2\le \rho_\delta^2/(4h_\delta))\ge 1-h_\delta^\zeta. The current reach estimate r_t=\Omega(h_t^2) cannot support this.
issues.overall_effect: The reach-stage guarantee (entry into the ridge tube by T-\delta with probability at least 1-e_\delta-o(1)) is not established; the informal Stage-1 theorem and the reach step of the main reach-align-slide claim lose their proof. The normal and tangent contraction theorems are only conditional on \Tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}\le T-\delta and do not supply entry.
issues.title: Stage-1 reach proof uses a reversed Gaussian concentration inequality with an exponentially small tube radius
issues.why_classification: The central reach guarantee is unproven: the key concentration step is invalid and the only available reach lower bound forces a tube radius too small for the entry event to have high probability. A repair needs a new reach lower bound and a corrected concentration argument, so no comparable version of the primary claim is supported by the source.

The main-text transfer theorem replaces it by d\delta, a strictly smaller (stronger) rate that the proof does not establish. The coefficient C_\delta^\parallel and the loss term are unchanged, so the defect is exactly the additive rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: within $B(a_\delta x_0^{(i)}, a_\delta \Delta/4)$, there exists a unique fixed point

issues.failure_explanation: The softmax ratio is bounded by \exp(-(d_j^2-d_i^2)/(2h_\delta)). Over the whole ball B(a_\delta x_0^{(i)},a_\delta\Delta/4), the minimal squared-distance gap is d_j^2-d_i^2\ge a_\delta^2\Delta^2/2 (attained at the boundary), not a_\delta^2\Delta^2. Hence the uniform bound should be \exp(-a_\delta^2\Delta^2/(4h_\delta)); the stated bound and the smallness conditions on h_\delta^{-1} use an exponent that is too large by a factor of 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \exp(-a_\delta^2\Delta^2/(2h_\delta)) by \exp(-a_\delta^2\Delta^2/(4h_\delta)) in the ratio estimate, the final distance bound, and the three smallness conditions on h_\delta^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative proximity rate of ridge points to the shrunk data points is overstated; the qualitative existence of exponentially close ridge points remains valid after correcting the constant.
issues.title: Ridge-point proximity bound has a factor-two error in the exponential rate
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local factor-of-two change in an exponent; the contraction-mapping argument, the ridge-curvature conclusion, and all downstream qualitative uses survive with the corrected constant.
